text:
mike: quick brain dump after last night's stale-read incident during demote+evict. I sketched an alternate: disk-backed replay + watermark handshake to avoid RAM soft-pinning.

tara: short timeline of the bug?

mike: old owner O1 accepted write W (inflight) -> slab reclaim evicted prefix -> demote completed -> new owner O2 served read -> pre-W returned. Root cause: inflight-only writes disappeared from the handoff path.

sasha: we've been iterating fence vs block vs read-retry. how does watermark+replay fit?

mike: idea: on demote, O1 writes a tiny replay-segment file (deltas for the prefix) to local staging and atomically publishes a watermark (max_admitted_seq) to control-plane. Demote ack only after watermark persisted. New owner sees handoff H = {epoch_next, required_seq}. If watermark >= required_seq -> safe. Else new owner pulls replay from O1 staging (or peers) and applies before serving reads.

lee: advantage: small durable disk write instead of holding large RAM pins. eviction can free memory but replay file survives on disk. we avoid memory churn.

tara: crash case: O1 crashes after creating replay but before watermark persist. Then new owner won't see watermark and will stall or trigger read-repair. So publish order must be: flush replay -> persist watermark -> ack demote.

sasha: storage location: /var/lib/redwood/prefix-replay/<prefix>-<epoch>-<uuid>. include manifest with digest, min_seq, max_seq. GC after TTL post-handoff.

mike: modes: strict (replicate replay to peer + persist watermark), balanced (persist watermark + local replay), fast (in-memory watermark beacon, best-effort). Default strict for enterprise.

lee: read-path optimization: new owner can attempt just-in-time replay pull for the specific read (apply minimal deltas) with T_read timeout to reduce full stalls. If timeout, fall back to stall or read-repair per tenant policy.

tara: telemetry: replay_created, watermark_persist_latency, replay_pull_latency, demote_stall_count, handoff_trace_id. Add canary flag to control replay-protect vs legacy soft-pin.

sasha: eviction changes: protect replay files (small disk footprint) during demote; avoid deleting staging until watermark confirmed and TTL expired. That reduces RAM pin but requires GC changes.

mike: tests: chaos scenario demote+slab+crash+slow-writes; validate no stale reads across modes. Add opctl commands in runbook to inspect replay files and force replay push to peer.

canary-bot: scheduled canary job CR-99: "watermark-replay-handoff" with memory vs latency benchmarks.

lee: sounds promising. main risk is IO/GC complexity and edge-case of watermark acknowledged but replay not durable. We'll require atomic flush+persist.

tara: agree. prefer strict-by-default, expose balanced/fast as tenant flags later.

mike: action items: prototype replay writer + atomic watermark persist (mike, 1w); Sasha: draft control-plane API + manifest schema (3d); Lee: add telemetry + canary toggles (2d); Tara: update runbook + opctl snippets (2d).

sasha: adding note: keep manifest minimal to avoid control-plane pressure (digest, seq-range, size).

mike: ok I'll open the PR with prototype and canary plan. closing thread.
